I mean, maybe? Probably. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like... like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. 

My badge is actually cracked right down the middle, by the way. I caught it in the car door a couple of weeks ago. I was rushing because I was running late, and the wind was blowing so hard it just ripped the door right out of my hand. The lanyard got caught in the latch mechanism. The gift shop has all this random stuff, like stuffed bears with little stethoscopes and these overpriced greeting cards. I bought a card there once for my coworker's baby shower, but I ended up smudging the ink when I signed it because I used a gel pen. I hate gel pens. They always smear if you're left-handed, which I am. My third-grade teacher tried to make me write with my right hand, actually. She used to tap my knuckles with a ruler if I picked up a pencil with my left. It was a wooden ruler with the metal edge, the kind that really stings...

But, um, anyway. Yeah, I think it's tied to that. That heavy feeling just sort of sits in my stomach, and it makes the thought of eating seem exhausting.

To answer your question, it's the enjoyment. I just don't feel any pleasure from those things anymore, so I just sit there with my spreadsheet because there's no point in trying to do anything else.\n\nDoctor: Do you think you would enjoy those activities again if your mood improved?\n\nPatient: I don't know. Maybe? It's hard to imagine right now. I keep thinking about how I used to run up in Van Cortlandt Park, take my camera out, play chess with Mark... but now I just tell myself there's no point to any of it. I just sit at home scrolling on my phone or staring at that budget spreadsheet. \n\nI really need to fix my phone, actually. The screen is cracked right across the middle. I dropped it when I was getting out of my friend Sarah's car last month. Sarah drives this ancient Honda Civic that smells like wet dog because she takes her golden retriever, Buster, everywhere. Buster is huge, like ninety pounds, and he sheds everywhere. I wore black pants in her car once and it was a total disaster. I had to buy one of those lint rollers with the sticky tape, you know? The ones where you have to peel the layer off when it gets full, but sometimes you peel off two layers by mistake and waste a perfectly good sheet. I hate wasting things. My dad was always big on not wasting anything. He used to save the rubber bands from the newspaper delivery and keep them on the doorknob. The doorknob was this old brass thing that was always freezing cold in the winter...\n\nBut yeah, I don't know if I'd enjoy those things again. Right now, I just sit at home because there's no point.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of appetite is more because of how you're feeling inside or because of physical sensations in your body?\n\nPatient: I think it's mostly how I'm feeling inside, honestly. It's like... my eating has gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift at work. I buy those Nature Valley ones, the oats and honey kind, but they are so crumbly. You take one bite and there are crumbs everywhere. I tried eating one in the breakroom last week and I had to sweep the floor afterward. The broom in the breakroom has this bright yellow handle, which always reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen. She painted her cabinets this awful mustard yellow back in the seventies, and it just stayed that way forever. She had these linoleum floors with a floral pattern that always looked slightly dirty no matter how much you mopped them. She used to use Pine-Sol, the original scent. It smells so strong, almost chemical. I can't stand strong smells anymore. \n\nBut yeah, my scrubs have been hanging loose on me lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. I just don't have the desire to eat.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel distressed by your lack of appetite?\n\nPatient: I mean, I guess it bothers me a little? It's just frustrating because, like I said, my eating is just so off. Some days I barely get down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging loose on me now. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. It's actually kind of annoying because I just bought a new set of scrubs a few months ago. They were the Cherokee brand, you know, the ones with the extra pockets on the cargo pants? I need the pockets for my pens and my notepad. I always use those Pilot G2 pens, the 0.7 millimeter ones. The fine point ones feel too scratchy on the paper, but the 0.7 is just right. The ink flows really smoothly. Although, if you're left-handed, they tend to smudge. My sister is left-handed, and she always complained about getting ink on the side of her hand when we were in school. She used to write with her hand hooked all the way around the top of the paper. It looked so uncomfortable. She ended up becoming an accountant, so she types mostly now anyway. She works for this big firm downtown, on the 42nd floor...\n\nBut um, yeah, I'm not trying to lose weight, so it is a little distressing that my clothes don't fit right anymore.\n\nDoctor: Are you avoiding food because you're worried about gaining weight if you eat normally again?\n\nPatient: No, no, not at all. I'm really not trying to lose weight. Like I said, it's just that my eating is so off right now. I just can't seem to manage more than a coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift. And now my scrubs are all baggy, which is a pain because they're the Cherokee ones. The fabric on those is usually so sturdy, you know? They hold up well in the wash. My washing machine has been making this awful clanking noise during the spin cycle lately, though. I think it's off balance, or maybe one of the shock absorbers is worn out. I watched a YouTube video on how to fix it, but you have to take the whole front panel off. The guy in the video made it look so easy, but he had all the right tools laid out on this pristine workbench. My garage is a total mess right now. I've been meaning to organize it, but I just end up staring at all the boxes. There's a box of my old vinyl records out there... I haven't listened to them in years. \n\nBut yeah, I'm definitely not avoiding food to stay thin or anything. I just don't have the appetite.\n\nDoctor: Do you think you would start eating more if you knew you wouldn't gain weight?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think so, because it really isn't about the weight at all. I know I sound like a broken record, but that's honestly what brought me in here in the first place—my eating has just gotten so completely off. I'm really not trying to lose weight, but I'm still just forcing down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are practically falling off me. \n\nSpeaking of the coffee, I usually stop at the Speedway on 4th street to get it on my way in. Their machines are always half broken. You press the button for French Vanilla and regular comes out. And they use those really flimsy paper cups, you know? If you don't grab one of those cardboard sleeves, you'll burn your hand off. I burned my thumb pretty bad on a cup of hot chocolate once when I was a teenager. We were camping up near the lake. The water up there is so clear, but it's freezing cold even in July. My dad used to make us go swimming at six in the morning. He said it built character, but I just remember shivering so hard my teeth hurt. He had this old green Coleman stove we used to boil the water on... \n\nBut yeah, no, knowing I wouldn't gain weight wouldn't change anything, because that's not why I'm not eating.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your lack of appetite is more related to your emotional state or to how your body physically feels?\n\nPatient: I think it's... it's definitely more about my emotional state. It's just this constant, heavy, hollow feeling, you know? Most mornings I wake up and it's like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. It's just this weight. \n\nSpeaking of my badge, the clip on it broke last week. It's one of those retractable ones, you know, with the string that pulls out so you can swipe the door sensors? The plastic part that snaps over your shirt pocket just snapped right in half. I had to use a safety pin to hold it on for the rest of the shift. Safety pins are so useful, though. My grandmother used to keep a whole jar of them on her sewing table, all different sizes. She had this beautiful old Singer sewing machine, the kind with the cast iron foot pedal. She used to make all her own curtains. They were always these heavy floral patterns that smelled like mothballs. Mothballs are such a strange smell, aren't they? They remind me of the attic in my childhood home. We had this big unfinished attic where we stored all the Christmas decorations. The tree always went up the day after Thanksgiving...\n\nBut um, yeah, I think it's the heavy feeling in the mornings that just ruins my appetite. I just don't care about eating when I feel like that."
